title: A corrupt base state file makes the gate unrepairable through a PR (DEC-213 (a2))
description:
Filed from finding 4 of the Stage 1 review of opum-ai/test-skills#46 and built under opum-doc DEC-213 (a2), read from opum-doc .quest/planning.json at dev.

PROBLEM. A quarantine or probation file that is corrupt at the BASE ref fails every PR against that base, including the PR that repairs it, so the condition cannot be repaired through the gate.

RULING. The HEAD copy is what DEC-213 item 1 guards: an unparseable head copy remains the named violation. An unparseable BASE copy, with a parseable head copy, is NOT a violation. The base is treated as empty, so every head entry counts as NEW and must meet the new-entry rules: owner and issue link, a listed approver where the level requires one, and a probation entry is uncertified without a matrix. That fails toward strict, the same shape as DEC-213 (a1). The report carries an info line naming the unreadable base file and saying its entries were treated as newly added.

PROOF, three ways:
- a corrupt base with a compliant head passes and names the base file;
- a corrupt base with a head entry lacking an owner fails on that entry;
- a corrupt head fails as before.

TEST SLOTS. Fold the proofs into existing parametrized or git-fixture cases where the shapes allow. Any new collected case is a measured slot request through the leader, sized under DEC-195's bar; the cap stays 95.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A base copy of either state file that cannot be parsed, with a parseable head, is not a violation: the head entries earn only the new-entry rules, and the run's info names the unreadable base file.
An unparseable head copy still fails by name as before.
The three proofs from DEC-213 (a2) are covered without adding a collected test case.

plan: 1. Split the head and base state-file loads so a corrupt base cannot abort the head load.
2. Treat an unparseable base copy as empty, add an info line naming the base file, and let every head entry meet the new-entry rules.
3. Keep an unparseable head copy a named violation.
4. Fold the three proofs into existing tests where the shapes allow; bring a measured slot request before any new collected case.
5. Run the suite and the repo gate locally, prove the behaviour both ways, open the PR, hold for a Stage 1 unit.
implementationNotes:
MEASURED, 2026-10-20, branch fix/TS-36-unreadable-base-state-file at ec0d837, before review. Ruling read from the record, not the relay: opum-doc .quest/planning.json at dev, DEC-213 (a2), decided from gate.py at c1886adc lines 398-413. Neither arm as offered: the HEAD copy stays the named violation; a corrupt BASE copy with a parseable head is NOT a violation, reads as empty, and every head entry must meet the new-entry rules; the report names the base file; proved both ways as listed.

IMPLEMENTATION. The head and base loads are now separate. An unparseable head copy still raises into the named violation. A base copy that will not parse goes through _load_base_list, which returns [] and appends an info line to info["unreadable_base_state_files"] naming the file, the kind and the parse error and saying its entries were treated as newly added. Because the base reads empty, every head entry counts as new and the existing owner/issue, approver and uncertified-demotion rules apply unchanged, which fails toward strict.

EVIDENCE. Full PR-tier suite: 95 passed, 8 deselected — the same count as the baseline, so no slot was spent and no test id moved. Repo gate in the CI shape (--junit report.xml --base origin/dev): PASS at R4 Strict, baseline_measured 95, growth 0, new_quarantine 0, new_probation 0.

PROOFS, folded into test_a_new_quarantine_entry_without_owner_and_issue_is_flagged and test_a_new_probation_entry_without_a_matrix_is_flagged, no new collected case:
1. corrupt base plus a compliant head passes, and the info names the unreadable file (quarantine and probation);
2. corrupt base plus a head entry with no owner still fails with quarantine_entry, and the same probation entry is still uncertified_demotion;
3. a corrupt head still fails by name, covered by the inverted test from TS-30.

MUTATION PROOFS, both arms with skills/test-audit/scripts/__pycache__ cleared. M1, the pre-(a2) behaviour restored by letting the base parse error propagate: both tests fail with StateFileError raised from gate.py:219. M2, base read as empty but no info line: both tests fail with KeyError unreadable_base_state_files. Restored: both pass.
finalSummary: An unparseable state file at the BASE ref no longer makes the gate unrepairable: it is not a violation, it reads as empty, and every head entry counts as newly added so the owner/issue, approver and uncertified-demotion rules still apply (DEC-213 (a2)). Head behaviour from TS-30 is unchanged: an unparseable head copy is still the named unreadable_state_file violation. The run info now carries unreadable_base_state_files, naming each base file, its kind and parse error, and saying its entries were treated as newly added. Proofs are folded into the two existing new-entry tests for both kinds, adding no collected case: suite 95 passed, baseline unchanged at 95, repo gate PASS at R4 Strict with baseline_measured 95 and growth 0. Mutation proofs: restoring the pre-(a2) behaviour fails both tests with StateFileError; dropping the info line fails both with KeyError unreadable_base_state_files; restored, both pass, with __pycache__ cleared on every arm.
